chapters.t: PART I — ENGINEERING MATHEMATICS & NUMERICAL METHODS
b: Covers the BSc mathematics courses on your Drive — Linear Algebra (1st sem), Differential Equations & Probability and Statistics (3rd sem), Numerical Analysis (4th sem) and MATLAB — at the level asked in engineering competitive tests (NTS/PPSC/FPSC/WAPDA, GATE-style).
Types: Symmetric (A = Aᵀ), skew-symmetric (A = −Aᵀ, diagonal zero), orthogonal (AᵀA = I, det = ±1), singular (det = 0), idempotent (A² = A), nilpotent (Aᵏ = 0), Hermitian.
Determinant facts: det(AB) = det A·det B; det(kA) = kⁿ det A; det(Aᵀ) = det A; swapping two rows changes sign; triangular → product of diagonal.
Rank: Number of non-zero rows in echelon form; Ax = b consistent iff rank(A) = rank([A|b]); unique if rank = n; infinite solutions if rank < n.
Eigenvalues: det(A − λI) = 0; Σλ = trace(A); Πλ = det(A); symmetric matrices have real eigenvalues & orthogonal eigenvectors; eigenvalues of triangular matrix = diagonal entries.
Cayley–Hamilton: Every square matrix satisfies its own characteristic equation (used to find A⁻¹ & powers).
Engineering use: Stiffness matrices (symmetric, positive definite), eigenvalue problems for natural frequencies & buckling, principal stresses.
Sum of eigenvalues = trace; product = determinant. A matrix is singular iff one eigenvalue is zero.
Maxima/minima: f′(x) = 0 and f″(x) < 0 → maximum; f″ > 0 → minimum. Two variables: rt − s² > 0 with r < 0 → max.
Standard limits: lim sin x/x = 1; lim (1 + 1/n)ⁿ = e; L'Hôpital for 0/0, ∞/∞.
Integration: ∫ uv dx by parts; definite-integral property ∫₀ᵃ f(x) dx = ∫₀ᵃ f(a − x) dx; even function ∫₋ₐᵃ = 2∫₀ᵃ, odd → 0.
Vector operators: Gradient ∇φ (vector, normal to surface); divergence ∇·F (scalar; 0 → solenoidal); curl ∇×F (0 → irrotational); ∇×∇φ = 0, ∇·(∇×F) = 0.
Theorems: Green (line ↔ area), Stokes (line ↔ surface, curl), Gauss divergence (surface ↔ volume).
Divergence-free = solenoidal (incompressible flow); curl-free = irrotational (potential flow).
Order & degree: Order = highest derivative; degree = power of highest derivative (after removing radicals).
First-order methods: Separable; homogeneous (y = vx); exact (∂M/∂y = ∂N/∂x); linear dy/dx + Py = Q (integrating factor e^∫P dx); Bernoulli.
Linear 2nd order, constant coefficients: Auxiliary eq. am² + bm + c = 0: real distinct → C₁e^(m₁x) + C₂e^(m₂x); repeated → (C₁ + C₂x)e^(mx); complex α ± iβ → e^(αx)(C₁cos βx + C₂sin βx).
Particular integrals: Undetermined coefficients / variation of parameters; resonance when forcing frequency equals natural frequency (multiply by x).
Engineering examples: Beam deflection EI y″ = M(x); SDOF vibration mü + cu̇ + ku = p(t); Euler column y″ + (P/EI)y = 0; consolidation (PDE ∂u/∂t = cv∂²u/∂z²).
PDE classification: A u_xx + B u_xy + C u_yy: B² − 4AC < 0 elliptic (Laplace), = 0 parabolic (heat/consolidation), > 0 hyperbolic (wave).
Laplace transform: L{1} = 1/s, L{eᵃᵗ} = 1/(s − a), L{sin at} = a/(s² + a²), L{f′} = sF(s) − f(0).
Heat & consolidation equations are parabolic; wave equation hyperbolic; Laplace equation (seepage flow net) elliptic.
Fig. 4.1 — Standard normal curve and the 68–95–99.7 rule.
Central tendency: Mean, median, mode; empirical relation Mode ≈ 3 Median − 2 Mean.
Dispersion: Range, variance σ² = Σ(x − x̄)²/n (sample uses n − 1), standard deviation, coefficient of variation CV = σ/x̄ (used for concrete quality control & rain-gauge networks).
Probability rules: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B); independent: P(A ∩ B) = P(A)P(B); conditional P(A|B) = P(A ∩ B)/P(B); Bayes' theorem.
Binomial: P(x) = ⁿCₓ pˣ qⁿ⁻ˣ; mean np, variance npq.
Poisson: P(x) = e^(−λ) λˣ/x!; mean = variance = λ (rare events — accidents, floods).
Normal: z = (x − μ)/σ; 68.3% within ±1σ, 95.4% ±2σ, 99.7% ±3σ; 1.645σ one-sided 95% (characteristic concrete strength f_ck = f_m − 1.65s).
Other distributions: Exponential (memoryless; mean 1/λ), uniform, log-normal (hydrology), Gumbel EV-I (floods, wind).
Correlation & regression: r between −1 and +1; least-squares line y = a + bx with b = Σ(x−x̄)(y−ȳ)/Σ(x−x̄)²; R² = proportion of variance explained.
Hypothesis testing: Null H₀ vs H₁; Type I error (reject true H₀, α), Type II (accept false H₀, β); t-test (small samples), χ² (goodness of fit), F-test (variances), p-value < α → reject H₀.
Characteristic strength = mean − 1.65 × SD (5% of results may fall below it).

chapters.t: Numerical Analysis — Errors & Roots of Equations
b: Errors: Round-off (finite digits), truncation (series/step approximation); absolute, relative, percentage error; significant figures.
Bisection: Bracketing, always converges, linear (halves interval each step): n ≥ log₂((b − a)/ε).
Regula falsi (false position): Bracketing with linear interpolation; faster than bisection but one end may stagnate.
Fig. 5.1 — Newton–Raphson iterations converge quadratically near a simple root.
Newton–Raphson: xₙ₊₁ = xₙ − f(xₙ)/f′(xₙ); quadratic convergence; fails if f′ ≈ 0. Square root of N: xₙ₊₁ = ½(xₙ + N/xₙ).
Secant: Uses two previous points, no derivative; order ≈ 1.618.
Fixed-point iteration: x = g(x) converges if |g′(x)| < 1 near the root.
Orders of convergence: bisection 1 (linear), secant 1.618, Newton–Raphson 2 (quadratic).

chapters.t: Numerical Analysis — Linear Systems, Interpolation, Integration & ODEs
b: Direct methods: Gauss elimination (with partial pivoting), Gauss–Jordan (→ identity; gives inverse), LU decomposition (Doolittle, Crout), Cholesky (symmetric positive definite — stiffness matrices).
Iterative methods: Jacobi, Gauss–Seidel (uses latest values, faster); converge if matrix is diagonally dominant; SOR for acceleration.
Interpolation: Newton forward/backward differences (equal spacing), Lagrange (unequal spacing), Newton divided differences; cubic splines.
Curve fitting: Least squares (linear, polynomial, exponential via log transform).
Fig. 6.1 — Trapezoidal rule vs Simpson's 1/3 rule.

Numerical integration: Trapezoidal: (h/2)[y₀ + 2(y₁ + … + yₙ₋₁) + yₙ] (error O(h²)); Simpson 1/3: (h/3)[y₀ + 4Σodd + 2Σeven + yₙ] (n even, O(h⁴)); Simpson 3/8 (n multiple of 3); Gauss quadrature (n points exact to degree 2n − 1).
Numerical differentiation: Forward difference O(h); central difference (y₁ − y₋₁)/2h is O(h²).
ODE solvers: Euler (first order, O(h)), modified Euler/Heun (2nd order), Runge–Kutta 4th order (most used, O(h⁴)), predictor–corrector (Milne, Adams).
Engineering use: Simpson's rule for areas/volumes (earthwork — prismoidal formula is Simpson's rule), Newton–Raphson in nonlinear analysis, Gauss quadrature in FEM, RK4 in dynamics & routing.
Simpson's 1/3 rule needs an even number of intervals; it is exact for polynomials up to degree 3.

chapters.t: Computing for Civil Engineers — MATLAB, SAP2000/ETABS & BIM
b: MATLAB basics: Matrix-based (MATrix LABoratory); A\b solves linear systems; eig(A) eigenvalues; ode45 (RK 4/5) for ODEs; polyfit/polyval for curve fitting; trapz & integral for integration; scripts (.m) & functions; plot/subplot for graphs.

SAP2000 / ETABS: CSI FE programs — frames (SAP2000 general structures & bridges, ETABS buildings); define materials & sections → draw → assign supports/loads → load combinations → run → design check (ACI/AISC). Rigid diaphragms, P-Δ, response spectrum & time history.
SAFE / CSiBridge: SAFE — slabs & foundations (punching, strip design); CSiBridge — bridge modelling with moving loads.

BIM: Building Information Modelling — 3D model with data; dimensions: 3D (geometry), 4D (time/schedule), 5D (cost), 6D (sustainability/energy), 7D (facility management). Tools: Revit, Navisworks (clash detection), Tekla (steel/RC detailing), ArchiCAD; IFC = open exchange format; LOD 100–500.

GIS & others: ArcGIS/QGIS (watersheds, land use), HEC-RAS (river hydraulics), HEC-HMS (rainfall–runoff), PLAXIS (geotech FEM), Primavera P6 & MS Project (scheduling), AutoCAD Civil 3D (roads, earthwork).
BIM 4D = time (scheduling), 5D = cost. Clash detection is a key BIM benefit (Navisworks).
